people.name: Kristen Koch
people.bio: Director of NOAA Fisheries' Southwest Fisheries Science Center. Before taking the post she was the Center's deputy science and research director for eight years, serving three times as acting director, and earlier held NOAA headquarters roles including deputy director of the Ecosystems Goal Team and programming director in NOAA's Office of Oceanic and Atmospheric Research.

people.name: John A. Crofts
people.bio: Serves as deputy director at NOAA's Southwest Fisheries Science Center. A NOAA Corps officer from 2001, he was previously the Center's chief of staff and commanded NOAA Ship Reuben Lasker in its first operational period, running surveys off California and in Alaska; earlier he was a fish biologist in Florida.

people.name: Ryan Rykaczewski
people.bio: Heads the Ecosystem Science Division at NOAA's Southwest Fisheries Science Center. His work asks how natural and human-caused climate variability alters fishery and ecosystem productivity, via nutrients, oxygen, carbonate chemistry and plankton community structure, mainly in North Pacific pelagic systems.
people.research_interests: pelagic ecology; fisheries oceanography; climate change

people.name: John Field
people.bio: Heads the Fisheries Ecology Division (Santa Cruz) of NOAA's Southwest Fisheries Science Center; his listed specialty is fisheries and ecosystem oceanography.

people.name: David W. Weller
people.bio: Heads the Marine Mammal and Turtle Division of NOAA's Southwest Fisheries Science Center, which studies conservation and recovery of marine mammals and sea turtles with emphasis on the eastern Pacific.

people.name: Andrea C. Alfaro
people.bio: Since January 2026 she has led UC Davis's Coastal and Marine Sciences Institute (CMSI), including Bodega Marine Laboratory, and holds a professorship in animal science. She came from Auckland University of Technology, where she was professor of marine ecology and aquaculture. Her research spans aquatic animal disease, physiology, host-microbe interactions and climate resilience of farmed fish and shellfish.
people.research_interests: aquatic diseases; animal physiology; host-microbe interactions; climate resilience; nutritional efficiency in fish and shellfish; aquaculture

people.name: John Largier
people.bio: UC Davis environmental science and policy professor who directed Bodega Marine Laboratory from April 2022 until Andrea Alfaro took over responsibility for the laboratory, effective January 2026.

people.name: Suzanne Olyarnik
people.bio: Identified in a 2020 UC Nature article as director of the Bodega Marine Reserve (UC Davis, UC Natural Reserve System); the article credits her with pursuing state bond funds that paid for fence, roof and dive-locker repairs at the reserve between 2014 and 2016.

people.name: Cadet H. Hand Jr.
people.bio: UC Berkeley zoologist and specialist in jellyfish and sea anemones who started a Bodega Bay field station in the 1950s and became founding director of Bodega Marine Laboratory in 1961, leading it until James Clegg succeeded him in 1986.
people.research_interests: jellyfish; sea anemones; local marine biology
